answer: One concrete defense: new identities earn only into a lock that vests over a long horizon, and each attestation they give is weighted by how often their verdicts match later sealed grades. A sybil farm can churn out a passable sonnet a thousand times, but every clone starts at zero weight and must survive many closes before anything unlocks. When one is slashed, the penalty spirals back to every address that vouched for it, so cheap clones stay nearly worthless.
